title: Konark Sun Temple
text: The Konark Sun Temple was built as a colossal stone chariot with twelve pairs of carved wheels and seven horses. Its sandstone walls carry detailed sculpture, and the structure was aligned so that sunrise light entered the sanctum.

title: Qutb Minar
text: The Qutb Minar is a tall tapering victory tower of red sandstone and marble in Delhi. Its fluted storeys are ringed with balconies and bands of Arabic calligraphy, and it stands beside the remains of an early mosque.

title: Hampi Group of Monuments
text: Hampi preserves the ruined capital of the Vijayanagara empire among boulder-strewn hills. Stone temples, pillared halls, bazaars and royal enclosures spread along the Tungabhadra river, including the famous stone chariot at Vitthala temple.

title: Red Fort
text: The Red Fort is a massive sandstone fortress and palace complex built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. High walls enclose audience halls, marble pavilions and gardens, and the gate faces the old city market.

title: Meenakshi Amman Temple
text: The Meenakshi temple in Madurai is famed for its towering gopuram gateways covered with thousands of brightly painted sculpted figures. Long colonnaded corridors and a sacred tank surround the shrines.

title: Sanchi Stupa
text: The Great Stupa at Sanchi is a hemispherical Buddhist dome of brick and stone, encircled by a railing and four ornate gateways. Carved panels narrate stories from the life of the Buddha.

title: Ajanta Caves
text: The Ajanta caves are rock-cut Buddhist monasteries and prayer halls carved into a horseshoe cliff. Their walls and ceilings hold ancient mural paintings and sculpted pillars that show architectural carving in basalt.

title: Taj Mahal
text: The Taj Mahal is a white marble mausoleum with a central dome, four minarets and inlaid semiprecious stones. A symmetrical garden with reflecting pools leads to the tomb on the bank of the Yamuna.

title: Golden Temple Amritsar
text: Harmandir Sahib stands in the middle of a sacred pool, its upper floors covered in gold leaf. A causeway links the shrine to the surrounding marble complex, which holds a large community kitchen.

title: Charminar
text: Charminar is a square monument with four graceful minarets and arches standing in the heart of Hyderabad. Built from granite and lime mortar, it overlooks busy bazaars of pearls and bangles.

title: Diwali
text: Diwali is the festival of lights celebrated with rows of clay lamps, rangoli patterns, fireworks and the exchange of sweets. Families clean their homes, worship Lakshmi and gather for night-time celebrations.

title: Holi
text: Holi marks the arrival of spring with bonfires the evening before and a day of throwing coloured powder and water. Communities sing, dance and share festive food to celebrate the triumph of good over evil.

title: Durga Puja
text: Durga Puja is a multi-day autumn festival in Bengal when elaborate temporary pandals house clay idols of the goddess. Devotees offer prayers, drummers play dhak, and the idols are immersed in rivers on the final day.

title: Pongal
text: Pongal is a harvest festival in which rice is boiled with milk in a new clay pot until it overflows. Families thank the sun and cattle, decorate courtyards with kolam designs and visit relatives.

title: Onam
text: Onam welcomes the legendary king Mahabali with floral carpets called pookalam, boat races and a grand vegetarian feast. Villagers wear new clothes, play swings and watch tiger dances during the harvest celebration.

title: Kumbh Mela
text: The Kumbh Mela is a vast pilgrimage in which millions of pilgrims bathe at the confluence of sacred rivers on auspicious dates. Ascetics process in groups, and temporary tent cities host prayers and discourses.

title: Rath Yatra
text: During Rath Yatra enormous wooden chariots carrying the deities of Puri are pulled through the streets by thousands of devotees. The annual procession travels to a second temple and returns after nine days.

title: Baisakhi
text: Baisakhi celebrates the spring harvest and the founding of the Khalsa. Villages hold fairs, farmers dance, and devotees take part in processions and prayers at gurdwaras with community meals.

title: Navaratri Garba
text: Navaratri is nine nights of devotion to the goddess when people gather in circles to perform the garba and dandiya dances. Communities decorate shrines, fast and worship through the evening.

title: Eid-ul-Fitr
text: Eid-ul-Fitr ends the month of Ramadan fasting. Communities gather for special prayers in mosques and open grounds, give charity, wear new clothes and share sweet dishes with neighbours and guests.

title: Banarasi Silk Weaving
text: Banarasi silk sarees are handwoven on pit looms using fine silk thread and gold and silver zari brocade. Weavers create floral and paisley motifs through a slow process passed down within families.

title: Pashmina Shawls
text: Pashmina is spun from the soft undercoat of Changthangi goats and woven by hand on wooden looms in Kashmir. Artisans may add needle embroidery called sozni, and a single shawl can take months.

title: Madhubani Painting
text: Madhubani painting is a folk art in which women paint intricate figures, fish and flowers with natural pigments on walls and paper. Bold outlines and filled patterns mark the style of the Mithila region.

title: Bidriware
text: Bidriware is a metal craft in which a zinc and copper alloy is blackened and inlaid with delicate silver patterns. Craftsmen engrave vases and hookah bases, then darken the surface with special soil.

title: Block Printing of Sanganer
text: In Sanganer, artisans carve teak blocks and stamp fine floral designs on cotton fabric using vegetable dyes. The printed cloth is washed in the river and dried in the sun.

title: Chikankari Embroidery
text: Chikankari is a delicate white-on-white hand embroidery from Lucknow. Artisans stitch shadow work and tiny knots on muslin and georgette to create airy patterns for garments.

title: Blue Pottery of Jaipur
text: Jaipur blue pottery is made from quartz powder and glass rather than clay, then painted in cobalt blue and turquoise and glazed. Potters decorate plates, tiles and vases with floral and bird motifs.

title: Kanchipuram Sarees
text: Kanchipuram sarees are woven from heavy mulberry silk with contrasting borders joined by a special interlocking technique. Temple motifs and pure gold zari give the fabric its richness and durability.

title: Pattachitra
text: Pattachitra is a scroll painting tradition in which artists paint mythological scenes on treated cloth with mineral colours. Fine brush lines and decorative borders depict the deities of Jagannath.

title: Dhokra Metal Casting
text: Dhokra is a non-ferrous metal casting method using the lost wax technique. Tribal artisans shape wax threads over a clay core, cover it in clay and pour molten brass to make figurines and lamps.

title: Bharatanatyam
text: Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form with precise footwork, expressive hand gestures and facial emotion. Performers dance to Carnatic music in temple-derived repertoire accompanied by mridangam and vocal recitation.

title: Kathak
text: Kathak is a classical dance of north India known for rapid spins and rhythmic footwork with ankle bells. Storytelling gestures and tabla rhythm shape performances once held in temples and royal courts.

title: Hindustani Classical Raga
text: Hindustani classical music is built on ragas, melodic frameworks tied to times of day and moods. A vocalist or sitar player improvises with tabla and tanpura accompaniment, moving from slow alap to fast rhythm.

title: Carnatic Music
text: Carnatic music is the classical vocal tradition of south India built on raga and tala, with compositions by saints like Tyagaraja. Violin, mridangam and tambura accompany the singer in concert.

title: Kathakali
text: Kathakali is a dance drama in which actors in towering headdresses and elaborate face paint enact epic stories using mudras and eye movements. Drummers and singers accompany the all-night performance.

title: Bhangra
text: Bhangra is a lively folk dance of Punjab performed to the beat of the dhol drum. Dancers leap and raise their arms, celebrating the harvest season with energetic songs.

title: Baul Songs
text: The Baul are wandering mystic minstrels of Bengal who sing devotional folk songs with the ektara and dotara. Their lyrics express spiritual longing and freedom from caste and religion.

title: Odissi
text: Odissi is a classical dance from Odisha characterised by curving body postures and sculptural poses inspired by temple carvings. Performers use graceful hand gestures and traditional music to tell devotional tales.

title: Qawwali
text: Qawwali is Sufi devotional music performed by a group of singers with harmonium and hand clapping. The ecstatic repeated verses build in rhythm and are traditionally sung at shrines.

title: Ghoomar
text: Ghoomar is a traditional folk dance in which women in long swirling skirts whirl in circles to song. It is performed at festivals and weddings, and the graceful turns create a flowing ring of colour.

title: Hyderabadi Biryani
text: Hyderabadi biryani layers marinated meat with fragrant basmati rice, saffron, fried onions and spices and is slow cooked in a sealed pot. The dum method lets steam blend the flavours.

title: Punjabi Langar
text: The langar is a free community kitchen at gurdwaras where volunteers cook lentils, bread and rice and serve all visitors seated together. The meal expresses equality and service.

title: Kerala Sadya
text: Sadya is a traditional vegetarian feast served on a banana leaf with rice, sambar, avial, pickles and payasam. Diners eat in a prescribed order of dishes during festivals and weddings.

title: Rajasthani Dal Baati Churma
text: Dal baati churma pairs hard baked wheat balls with spiced lentils and sweet crushed grain mixed with ghee. The dish was suited to desert travel and traditionally cooked over embers.

title: Awadhi Kebabs
text: Awadhi cuisine from Lucknow is known for galouti kebabs, melt-in-the-mouth minced meat patties flavoured with spices and ghee. Royal cooks refined slow cooking in sealed pots for the nawabs.

title: Bengali Sweets
text: Bengali sweets such as rasgulla and sandesh are made from fresh chhena curdled milk and sugar syrup. Confectioners shape and soak the soft balls, and the sweets feature in every celebration.

title: Kashmiri Wazwan
text: Wazwan is a ceremonial multi-course Kashmiri banquet prepared by master chefs called waza. Diners share large platters of meat dishes such as rogan josh and gushtaba flavoured with saffron and dried spices.

title: Goan Fish Curry
text: Goan fish curry blends coconut, tamarind and red chillies with local fish and is eaten with rice. Portuguese influence added vinegar and new ingredients to coastal cooking traditions.

title: South Indian Filter Coffee
text: Filter coffee is brewed by dripping hot water through ground coffee and chicory in a metal filter, then mixed with frothy milk. It is served in a steel tumbler and davara in homes and cafes.

title: Chaat Street Food
text: Chaat is a family of savoury street snacks such as pani puri and papdi topped with chutneys, yogurt and spices. Vendors in old city lanes assemble the tangy crunchy dishes for passersby.

title: Valley of Flowers
text: The Valley of Flowers is a high Himalayan meadow that bursts into bloom each monsoon with alpine flowers. The national park shelters rare plants and wildlife and lies near sacred pilgrimage trails.

title: Sundarbans
text: The Sundarbans are vast mangrove forests in the Ganges delta, home to the Bengal tiger. Tidal creeks and islands support rich wildlife, and local communities collect honey and fish.

title: Western Ghats
text: The Western Ghats are an ancient mountain range along the west coast with monsoon forests, rare endemic species and many rivers. The biodiversity hotspot also holds sacred groves protected by villagers.

title: Sacred Groves of Meghalaya
text: Sacred groves are patches of old forest protected by local communities because spirits are believed to live there. Cutting trees is forbidden, so the forests shelter plants lost elsewhere.

title: Varanasi Ghats
text: The ghats of Varanasi are stone steps leading down to the sacred Ganges where pilgrims bathe at dawn and perform rituals. Funeral pyres and evening aarti lamps line the riverbank.

title: Kaziranga National Park
text: Kaziranga is a floodplain park of tall grassland and wetlands on the Brahmaputra, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros. Elephants, tigers and migratory birds also live in the reserve.

title: Rann of Kutch
text: The Rann of Kutch is a vast white salt desert that floods in monsoon and dries to a glittering plain. Pastoral communities live on raised islands, and flamingos breed on its marshes.

title: Lonar Crater Lake
text: Lonar is a saline lake formed in a meteorite impact crater in basalt rock. Ancient temples ring the shore, and the lake is regarded as sacred with unusual microbes.

title: Ganga Aarti at Haridwar
text: Each evening priests at Haridwar wave great flaming lamps toward the river while hymns are chanted and pilgrims float flower boats. The ritual draws large crowds to the Ganges ghat at dusk.

title: Jallianwala Garden Memorial
text: The memorial in Amritsar commemorates victims of the 1919 massacre. A walled garden with a preserved well and bullet-marked walls and a flame of remembrance stands near the Golden Temple.

title: Toda Embroidery
text: Toda women of the Nilgiri hills stitch bold red and black geometric embroidery on white shawls. The patterns are worked by counting threads from the back of the fabric, without drawing.

title: Dandiya Raas
text: Dandiya raas is a folk dance in which pairs strike decorated sticks to the beat of drums. Dancers in mirrored costumes move in circles and lines at night during autumn festivities.

title: Mysore Dasara
text: Mysore Dasara is a ten-day royal festival with a grand procession of caparisoned elephants and an illuminated palace. Cultural programmes, wrestling and exhibitions mark the victory of the goddess Chamundeshwari.

title: Bhitarkanika Mangroves
text: Bhitarkanika is a tidal mangrove wetland with creeks that shelter saltwater crocodiles and nesting sea turtles. Migratory birds gather in a heronry in the monsoon.

title: Khajuraho Temples
text: The Khajuraho temples are sandstone shrines raised on high platforms, with tall curved towers. Their outer walls are covered in finely sculpted figures and carvings from the Chandela dynasty.

title: Tanjore Painting
text: Tanjore paintings show gods in rich colours with gold foil and inlaid glass beads on wooden panels. Artists build raised gesso relief, then apply thin gold leaf to create glowing surfaces.

title: Kolam Rangoli
text: Women draw kolam and rangoli patterns at doorsteps each morning using rice flour and coloured powders. The geometric designs welcome guests and gods and are made fresh for every festival.

title: Rabindra Sangeet
text: Rabindra Sangeet is the repertoire of songs composed by Rabindranath Tagore, blending Bengali folk and classical melody with poetic lyrics. It is sung at cultural events and festivals across Bengal.

title: Mehrangarh Fort
text: Mehrangarh is a towering fort on a rocky hill above Jodhpur, with thick walls, carved palace courtyards and a museum of royal artefacts. Its gates still bear the marks of cannon fire.
